outputs: Texts generated for six genres (non-fiction, fiction, poetry, summarization, article, key-word text) using five decoding strategies
Machine-generated texts across six genres used for eye-tracking experiments
The paper investigates how different text types generated by LLMs influence human reading behavior, including eye movement patterns during reading.

changes_made.explanation: Removed redundant task entries (Dialogue Generation appeared twice, removed 'Other:' prefix for standard tasks), normalized model name format, and removed output description that was more about evaluation than generation.
No automatic metrics were used in this paper - evaluation was done exclusively through eye-tracking measures of human reading behavior.
No LLMs were used as judges/evaluators in this paper - LLMs were only used for text generation.

guideline: The study uses eye-tracking data collected from human readers while reading machine-generated texts across six genres, measuring cognitive effort through reading behavior such as fixation duration, regression, and re-reading times

changes_made.explanation: Human evaluation was conducted through eye-tracking experiments, and the extracted criteria accurately reflect the reading measures used in the study.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on evaluating NLG outputs through human eye-tracking experiments rather than automatic metrics. The extraction was generally accurate, but needed some cleanup of redundant task entries and model name normalization. The paper's main contribution is studying how different text types and decoding strategies affect human reading behavior of machine-generated texts.
